definition: Whether normalization is applied before or after each sublayer.
details: Whether normalization is applied before or after each sublayer. Pre-norm (used by nearly all modern LLMs) is far more stable at depth; post-norm (the original Transformer) can yield slightly better quality but is fragile to train.

explainer.lead: Pre-norm versus post-norm concerns whether normalization is applied before or after each sublayer in a transformer. It matters because pre-norm is far more stable at depth and is used by nearly all modern LLMs.

tiers.eli5: Like whether you tidy up before or after each task: doing it before keeps things from piling up as you go deeper.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers default to pre-norm in deep models for training stability; a pitfall is that post-norm, the original Transformer choice, can yield slightly better quality but is fragile to train.
tiers.paperLevel: The distinction is placement of normalization relative to each sublayer: pre-norm applies it before, post-norm after; pre-norm is far more stable at depth, while post-norm can give slightly better quality but is fragile to train.

explainer.example: A deep LLM places normalization before each sublayer to stay stable, whereas the original Transformer normalised after and was harder to train at depth.
